svg.title: Finite coefficient charts and the distinction between ordinary and derived points
svg.desc: For every smooth projective complex curve and connected reductive H, finite antipode-stable coefficient subcoalgebras define affine finite-type ordinary charts by explicit relation, coproduct and counit equations. Inclusions are closed, and the ordinary framed prestack is their filtered colimit. The square-zero ordinary coefficient stage and a polynomial triangular matrix family retain nilpotents. The projective-line derived framed point has a nonzero first loop over a degree-minus-two coefficient algebra.
svg.text: Ordinary restricted points from finite coefficient equations
Smooth projective complex X; connected reductive H; arbitrary ordinary coefficient algebras.
1. An actual finite affine chart — SCI.1–SCI.7
C_X = the representative-function Hopf algebra; 1 ∈ E, ΔE ⊂ E⊗E, S(E) = E.
O(H) = C[b₁,…,bₘ]/(r₁,…,rₛ); choose a basis e₁,…,e_d of E.
q_i = Σα x_iα e_α; impose r_j(q)=0, Δq_i = D_i(q⊗1,1⊗q), ε(q_i)=ε(b_i).
Y_E = Spec C[x_iα]/(these coefficient equations): finite type, nilpotents retained.
No condition here replaces an ordinary coefficient algebra by its reduced ring.
2. Closed inclusions and the ordinary quotient — SCI.8–SCI.10
E ⊂ E′: set the extra generator coefficients equal to zero.
Y_E ↪ Y_E′ is a closed embedding; Y^cl = colim_E Y_E.
Z^cl = colim_E [Y_E/H]_fpqc.
Every finite list of generator coefficients lies in one common E.
Conjugation preserves the matrix-generator span; the finite-stage condition descends.
3. A nonreduced stage is visible — SCI.17–SCI.18
Γ = Z, H = G_m, E = span{1,n}, with n(k)=k and Δn=n⊗1+1⊗n.
φ(t)=1+bn, φ(t⁻¹)=1+dn; b²=d²=0, b+d=0, bd=0.
Y_E = Spec C[b]/b²; monodromy at k is 1+kb for every integer k.
This is the ordinary first nilpotent thickening at the character 1.
Its reduced point discards these square-zero ordinary families.
4. Polynomial entries can stay in one coefficient stage — SCI.14–SCI.16
A=C[s], λ≠0 fixed; M(s)=λI₂+sE₁₂ and (sE₁₂)²=0.
M(s)^k = λ^k I₂ + kλ^(k−1)sE₁₂, including every negative k.
C[M,M⁻¹] = span_C{I₂,sE₁₂}: finite over the original C.
E = span{1, λ^k, kλ^k, λ^(−k), kλ^(−k)} contains all matrix coefficients.
Γ=Z is a coefficient-group example, not the fundamental group of every curve.
5. Ordinary charts do not determine derived loops — SCI.19–SCI.20
X=P¹, H=G_m: the ordinary framed prestack is a point.
A=C[δ]/δ², |δ|=−2: Y(A)=Map_CAlg(Sym(C[1]),A).
π₀ is a singleton, π₁=Cδ, and π_i=0 for i>1.
A nonzero loop sends v of degree −1 to δ dt; its interval integral is δ.
The terminal derived affine has no such loop.
Full DG charts additionally require coherent deformation, cotangent and effectivity arguments.
Proof locators: §§3.112–3.118. Coefficient framework: AGKRRV, arXiv:2010.01906v2.
